To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gradual increase of gravity supports learning, despite the necessary adjustments of motor actions, and that the learning behaviour is influenced by the interaction of skill acquisition and adaptation processes.

1) the gradual increase in task difficulty during skill acquisition supports skill acquisition, although overall improvement is interrupted by necessary adjustments to changing system dynamics; 2) the gradual increase of difficulty supports learning, although overall improvement in performance is interrupted by the necessary adjustments to changing task dynamics; and 3) the gradual increase supports learning, although it does not prevent short-term degradational performance.
the interaction of reward-based learning and adaptation to changes in system dynamics is crucial for the optimization of skill acquisition schedules in virtual reality environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, how to design a learning process in order to optimize learning efficiency.
learning in real life and its underlying mechanisms.
the interaction of different learning processes and their influence on the acquisition of a motor skill.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the learning processes of reward-based skill learning, motor adaptation and learning from experience interact with each other, which has implications for the development of training schedules.
the learning process is a complex process and that it is not possible to describe it in a linear manner.
the interaction of learning processes can be beneficial for skill acquisition, but also can lead to a degradation in performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
learning is a complex interaction between multiple processes.
learning to control is not only about the acquisition of a skill, but also about adapting to changing system dynamics.
learning to control with gradually changed system dynamics is a complex process, in which several learning mechanisms are active and interact.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning to control a system with gradually changing dynamics is more efficient than learning on a system with constant dynamics, but with the same final difficulty level.
the interaction between learning processes is an important factor to take into account when designing learning schedules for skill acquisition.
the gradual increase of gravity supports learning despite the required adjustments to changes in system dynamics.
